A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 23-page versions of the same research work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original ReSynth experiments, a 50-participant preference study, qualitative comparisons, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds quantitative ablation results, a full-body generation-only comparison, and computational efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The three-region segmentation, LBS deformation, part-aware free-form generator, and training losses remain unchanged. FreeCloth is a new name; the added experimental controls do not modify the proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same five ReSynth skirt/dress subjects, multi-subject interpolation experiments, and non-skirt clothing demonstrations. The added controls and efficiency measurements do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: POP, SkiRT, and FITE remain the external baselines. V2 adds a full-body generation-only comparator in Figure B10, beyond the lower-body generation-only control already present and retained in Figure 6.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an efficiency evaluation reporting FPS, FLOPs, and parameter counts, with inference measured on an RTX 3090 at batch size 1. It also adds the full-body generation-only control setting. Existing data splits and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section B.6 extends the existing hybrid-paradigm ablation with quantitative deformation-only results across five subjects (Table B3) and a full-body generation-only comparison (Figure B10). V1 already tested deformation-only and lower-body generation-only variants qualitatively; the existing patch-count, clothing-cut, and failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports model-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's added results continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates without uncertainty measures.

E6.justification: Tables 2, B1, and B2 retain their original scores. New Table B3 reports deformation-only averages of FID 56.23 and MSE 2.73; Table B4 adds computational results, including FreeCloth's 64.1 FPS and 10.83 million parameters. Figure B10 adds qualitative evidence of coarse, noisy full-body generation.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, transformations, and loss equations (1–13) are unchanged. V2 adds no formal assumptions, proofs, theorems, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about hybrid modeling, structure-aware free-form generation, and superior visual quality for challenging loose clothing. Naming the framework FreeCloth does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V2 explains why lower-leg poses influence short skirts despite lacking direct coverage (A.1), clarifies the interaction between branches without clothing-cut guidance (4.2), and adds efficiency interpretations (B.7). The temporal, penetration, and seam limitations remain in renumbered Section B.8.

D1.justification: V2 supplies hardware and batch-size information for its new timing comparison. Section 4.2 also clarifies that the existing clothing-cut ablation uses the default UV map and deforms body points in loose regions. Core architecture details, training hyperparameters, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 72 references and substantive positioning relative to LBS-based methods, LBS-free animation, and point-cloud representations are retained. Removing a redundant citation group in B.4 does not alter the research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 adds the FreeCloth name, revises affiliations and correspondence information, adds an acknowledgment, and makes localized prose corrections and clarifications. Appendix subsections expand, but the overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables B3–B4 and the full-body ablation Figure B10. Existing appendix figures are repositioned and renumbered, and the title-page layout changes. The original visual comparisons and main table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's qualitative hybrid controls, v2 adds useful quantitative validation and a full-body control, while Table B4 makes computational costs assessable. These improve supporting evidence without changing the headline findings. Precision is weakened slightly by the ablation text/table MSE mismatch (2.74 versus 2.73) and the broad no-extra-overhead interpretation despite mixed speed and FLOP comparisons. The evidential gains outweigh these limited issues.
